newsitem.title: USA: Durakon sees further growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Durakon sees further growth in 1997.

text.p: Durakon Industries Inc said Monday it expects to post further profitability and continued sales growth in 1997, with key products and contracts seen boosting results.
"In 1997, we expect further progress in profitability and continued sales growth," David Wright, president and chief executive officer, said in a statement.
Wright cited Durakon's contract to supply bedliners to the Ford Motor Co, an expanded line of vehicle accessories, and a complete year of sales from a new line of medium-duty tow trucks.
Wright said the company's relationship with Ford could become one of the most significant in company history.

"Although start-up costs for the Ford project will affect first quarter results, full-scale service is scheduled to begin in March and should create the potential for improvements to 1997 sales and earnings," Wright said.
Earlier, the company reported fourth quarter earnings of $0.31 a share versus a loss of $0.69 a share last year, which included charges for the closure of its ZZ Wheelz unit.

The company said its effort to improve its cost structure in the vehicle accessories segment also made progress. Gross margin for the segment rose to 29 percent from 27 percent in 1995, and operating margin was substantially higher, Durakon said. The company said competition in the aftermarket hurt selling prices.

"The new Ford business and several new products, as well as continued emphasis on reducing our cost structure, are beginning to place Durakon's sales and earnings on a stronger, more consistent growth track," Wright said.
